verses.zh: 基列人耶弗他是个大能的勇士，是妓女的儿子。耶弗他是基列所生的。
verses.en: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a brave warrior. His mother was a prostitute, but Gilead was his father.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Now he was the son of a woman, a prostitute, and Gilead fathered Jephthah.”

verses.zh: 基列的妻也生了几个儿子：他妻所生的儿子长大了，就赶逐耶弗他，说：「你不可在我们父家承受产业，因为你是妓女的儿子。」
verses.en: Gilead’s wife also gave[NOTE:1] him sons. When his wife’s sons grew up, they made Jephthah leave and said to him, “You are not going to inherit any of our father’s wealth[NOTE:2] because you are another woman’s son.”
notes: Heb “bore.”
Heb “in the house of our father.”

verses.zh: 耶弗他就逃避他的弟兄，去住在陀伯地，有些匪徒到他那里聚集，与他一同出入。
verses.en: So Jephthah left[NOTE:1] his half brothers[NOTE:2] and lived in the land of Tob. Lawless men joined Jephthah’s gang and traveled with him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “fled from.”
Heb “brothers.”
Heb “Empty men joined themselves to Jephthah and went out with him.”

verses.zh: 过了些日子，亚扪人攻打以色列。
verses.en: It was some time after this when the Ammonites fought with Israel.

verses.zh: 亚扪人攻打以色列的时候，基列的长老到陀伯地去，要叫耶弗他回来；
verses.en: When the Ammonites attacked,[NOTE:1] the leaders[NOTE:2] of Gilead asked Jephthah to come back[NOTE:3] from the land of Tob.
notes: Heb “When the Ammonites fought with Israel.”
Or “elders.”
Heb “went to take Jephthah.”

verses.zh: 对耶弗他说：「请你来作我们的元帅，我们好与亚扪人争战。」
verses.en: They said,[NOTE:1] “Come, be our commander, so we can fight with the Ammonites.”
notes: Heb “to Jephthah.”

verses.zh: 耶弗他回答基列的长老说：「从前你们不是恨我、赶逐我出离父家吗？现在你们遭遇急难为何到我这里来呢？」
verses.en: Jephthah said to the leaders of Gilead, “But you hated me and made me leave[NOTE:1] my father’s house. Why do you come to me now, when you are in trouble?”
notes: Heb “Did you not hate me and make me leave?”

verses.zh: 基列的长老回答耶弗他说：「现在我们到你这里来，是要你同我们去，与亚扪人争战；你可以作基列一切居民的领袖。」
verses.en: The leaders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “That may be true,[NOTE:1] but now we pledge to you our loyalty.[NOTE:2] Come with us and fight with the Ammonites. Then you will become the leader[NOTE:3] of all who live in Gilead.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “therefore”; “even so.” For MT לָכֵן (lakhen, “therefore”) the LXX has an opposite reading, “not so,” which seems to be based on the Hebrew words לֹא כֵן (loʾ khen).
Heb “we have returned to you.” For another example of שׁוּב אֶל (shuv ʾel) in the sense of “give allegiance to,” see 1 Kgs 12:27b.

Then you will become the leader. The leaders of Gilead now use the word רֹאשׁ (roʾsh, “head, leader”), the same term that appeared in their original, general offer (see 10:18). In their initial offer to Jephthah they had simply invited him to be their קָצִין (qatsin, “commander”; v. 6). When he resists they must offer him a more attractive reward—rulership over the region. See R. G. Boling, Judges (AB), 198.
Heb “leader of us and all who live in Gilead.”

verses.zh: 耶弗他对基列的长老说：「你们叫我回去，与亚扪人争战，耶和华把他交给我，我可以作你们的领袖吗？」
verses.en: Jephthah said to the leaders of Gilead, “All right.[NOTE:1] If you take me back to fight with the Ammonites and the Lord gives them to me,[NOTE:2] I will be your leader.”[NOTE:3]
notes: “All right” is supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “places them before me.”

Some translate the final statement as a question, “will I really be your leader?” An affirmative sentence is preferable. Jephthah is repeating the terms of the agreement in an official manner. In v. 10 the leaders legally agree to these terms.

verses.zh: 基列的长老回答耶弗他说：「有耶和华在你我中间作见证，我们必定照你的话行。」
verses.en: The leaders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “The Lord will judge any grievance you have against us[NOTE:1] if we do not do as you say.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “The Lord will be the one who hears between us.” For the idiom שָׁמַע בַּיִן (shamaʿ bayin, “to hear between”), see Deut 1:16.
The Lord will judge…if we do not do as you say. The statement by the leaders of Gilead takes the form of a legally binding oath, which obligates them to the terms of the agreement.

verses.zh: 于是耶弗他同基列的长老回去，百姓就立耶弗他作领袖、作元帅。耶弗他在米斯巴将自己的一切话陈明在耶和华面前。
verses.en: So Jephthah went with the leaders of Gilead. The people made him their leader and commander. Jephthah repeated the terms of the agreement[NOTE:1] before the Lord in Mizpah.
notes: Heb “spoke all his words.” This probably refers to the “words” recorded in v. 9. Jephthah repeats the terms of the agreement at the Lord’s sanctuary, perhaps to ratify the contract or to emphasize the Gileadites’ obligation to keep their part of the bargain. Another option is to translate, “Jephthah conducted business before the Lord in Mizpah.” In this case, the statement is a general reference to the way Jephthah ruled. He recognized the Lord’s authority and made his decisions before the Lord.

verses.zh: 耶弗他打发使者去见亚扪人的王，说：「你与我有甚么相干，竟来到我国中攻打我呢？」
verses.en: Jephthah sent messengers to the Ammonite king, saying, “Why have[NOTE:1] you come against me to attack my land?”
notes: Heb “What to me and to you that…?”

verses.zh: 亚扪人的王回答耶弗他的使者说：「因为以色列人从埃及上来的时候占据我的地，从亚嫩河到雅博河，直到约旦河。现在你要好好地将这地归还吧！」
verses.en: The Ammonite king said to Jephthah’s messengers, “Because Israel stole[NOTE:1] my land when they[NOTE:2] came up from Egypt—from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and as far west as the Jordan.[NOTE:3] Now return it[NOTE:4] peaceably!”
notes: Or “took”; or “seized.”
Heb “he” (a collective singular).

Heb “from the Arnon to the Jabbok and to the Jordan.” The word “River” has been supplied in the translation with “Arnon” and “Jabbok,” because these are less familiar to modern readers than the Jordan.
The translation assumes a singular suffix (“[return] it”); the Hebrew text has a plural suffix (“[return] them”), which, if retained, might refer to the cities of the land.

verses.zh: 耶弗他又打发使者去见亚扪人的王，
verses.en: Jephthah sent messengers back to the Ammonite king

verses.zh: 对他说：「耶弗他如此说，以色列人并没有占据摩押地和亚扪人的地。
verses.en: and said to him, “This is what Jephthah says, ‘Israel did not steal[NOTE:1] the land of Moab and the land of the Ammonites.
notes: Or “take”; or “seize.”

verses.zh: 以色列人从埃及上来乃是经过旷野到红海，来到加低斯，
verses.en: When they left[NOTE:1] Egypt, Israel traveled[NOTE:2] through the desert as far as the Red Sea and then came to Kadesh.
notes: Heb “For when they went up from.”
Or “went.”

verses.zh: 就打发使者去见以东王，说：『求你容我从你的地经过。』以东王却不应允。又照样打发使者去见摩押王，他也不允准。以色列人就住在加低斯。
verses.en: Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, “Please allow us[NOTE:1] to pass through your land.” But the king of Edom rejected the request.[NOTE:2] Israel sent the same request to the king of Moab, but he was unwilling to cooperate.[NOTE:3] So Israel stayed at Kadesh.
notes: Heb “me.” (Collective Israel is the speaker.)
Heb “did not listen.”
Heb “Also to the king of Moab he sent, but he was unwilling.”

verses.zh: 他们又经过旷野，绕着以东和摩押地，从摩押地的东边过来，在亚嫩河边安营，并没有入摩押的境内，因为亚嫩河是摩押的边界。
verses.en: Then Israel[NOTE:1] went through the wilderness and bypassed the land of Edom and the land of Moab. They traveled east of the land of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon River;[NOTE:2] they did not go through Moabite territory (the Arnon was Moab’s border).
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Israel; the pronoun in the Hebrew text represents a collective singular) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 以色列人打发使者去见亚摩利王西宏，就是希实本的王，对他说：『求你容我们从你的地经过，往我们自己的地方去。』
verses.en: Israel sent messengers to King Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, “Please allow us to pass through your land to our land.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to my place.”

verses.zh: 西宏却不信服以色列人，不容他们经过他的境界，乃招聚他的众民在雅杂安营，与以色列人争战。
verses.en: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. He[NOTE:1] assembled his whole army,[NOTE:2] camped in Jahaz, and fought with Israel.
notes: Heb “Sihon.” The proper name (“Sihon”) has been replaced in the translation by the pronoun (“he”) because of English style; a repetition of the proper name here would be redundant in English.
Heb “all his people” (also in the following verse).

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的　神将西宏和他的众民都交在以色列人手中，以色列人就击杀他们，得了亚摩利人的全地：
verses.en: The Lord God of Israel handed Sihon and his whole army over to Israel, and they defeated them. Israel took[NOTE:1] all the land of the Amorites who lived in that land.
notes: That is, took as its own possession.

verses.zh: 从亚嫩河到雅博河，从旷野直到约旦河。
verses.en: They took all the Amorite territory from the Arnon River on the south to the Jabbok River on the north, from the desert in the east to the Jordan in the west.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from the Arnon to the Jabbok, and from the desert to the Jordan.” The word “River” has been supplied in the translation with “Arnon” and “Jabbok,” because these are less familiar to modern readers than the Jordan.

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的　神在他百姓以色列面前赶出亚摩利人，你竟要得他们的地吗？
verses.en: Since[NOTE:1] the Lord God of Israel has driven out[NOTE:2] the Amorites before his people Israel, do you think you can just take it from them?[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Now.”
Or “dispossessed.”
Heb “will you dispossess him [i.e., Israel; or possibly “it,” i.e., the territory]?” There is no interrogative marker in the Hebrew text.

verses.zh: 你的神基抹所赐你的地你不是得为业吗？耶和华―我们的　神在我们面前所赶出的人，我们就得他的地。
verses.en: You have the right to take what Chemosh your god gives you, but we will take the land of all whom the Lord our God has driven out before us.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Is it not so that what Chemosh your god causes you to possess, you possess, and all whom the Lord our God dispossesses before us we will possess?” Jephthah speaks of Chemosh as if he is on a par with the Lord God of Israel. This does not necessarily mean that Jephthah is polytheistic or that he recognizes the Lord as only a local deity. He may simply be assuming the Ammonite king’s perspective for the sake of argument. Other texts, as well as the extrabiblical Mesha inscription, associate Chemosh with Moab, while Milcom is identified as the god of the Ammonites. Why then does Jephthah refer to Chemosh as the Ammonite god? Ammon had likely conquered Moab and the Ammonite king probably regarded himself as heir of all territory formerly held by Moab. Originally Moab had owned the disputed territory (cf. Num 21:26-29), meaning that Chemosh was regarded as the god of the region (see R. G. Boling, Judges [AB], 203-4). Jephthah argues that Chemosh had long ago relinquished claim to the area (by allowing Sihon to conquer it), while the Lord had long ago established jurisdiction over it (by taking it from Sihon and giving it to Israel). Both sides should abide by the decisions of the gods which had stood firm for 300 years.

verses.zh: 难道你比摩押王西拨的儿子巴勒还强吗？他曾与以色列人争竞，或是与他们争战吗？
verses.en: Are you really better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he dare to quarrel with Israel? Did he dare to fight with them?[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew grammatical constructions of all three rhetorical questions indicate emphasis, which “really” and “dare to” are intended to express in the translation. sn Jephthah argues that the Ammonite king should follow the example of Balak, who, once thwarted in his attempt to bring a curse on Israel, refused to attack Israel and returned home (Num 22-24).

verses.zh: 以色列人住希实本和属希实本的乡村，亚罗珥和属亚罗珥的乡村，并沿亚嫩河的一切城邑，已经有三百年了；在这三百年之内，你们为甚么没有取回这些地方呢？
verses.en: Israel has been living in Heshbon and its nearby towns, in Aroer and its nearby towns, and in all the cities along the Arnon for 300 years! Why did you not reclaim them during that time?

verses.zh: 原来我没有得罪你，你却攻打我，恶待我。愿审判人的耶和华今日在以色列人和亚扪人中间判断是非。」
verses.en: I have not done you wrong,[NOTE:1] but you are doing wrong[NOTE:2] by attacking me. May the Lord, the Judge, judge this day between the Israelites and the Ammonites!’”
notes: Or “sinned against you.”
Or “evil.”

verses.zh: 但亚扪人的王不肯听耶弗他打发人说的话。
verses.en: But the Ammonite king disregarded[NOTE:1] the message sent by Jephthah.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “did not listen to.”
Heb “Jephthah’s words which he sent to him.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的灵降在耶弗他身上，他就经过基列和玛拿西，来到基列的米斯巴，又从米斯巴来到亚扪人那里。
verses.en: The Lord’s Spirit empowered[NOTE:1] Jephthah. He passed through Gilead and Manasseh and went[NOTE:2] to Mizpah in Gilead. From there he approached the Ammonites.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “was on.”
Heb “passed through.”
Heb “From Mizpah in Gilead he passed through [to] the Ammonites.”

verses.zh: 耶弗他就向耶和华许愿，说：「你若将亚扪人交在我手中，
verses.en: Jephthah made a vow to the Lord, saying, “If you really do hand the Ammonites over to me,

verses.zh: 我从亚扪人那里平平安安回来的时候，无论甚么人，先从我家门出来迎接我，就必归你，我也必将他献上为燔祭。」
verses.en: then whoever is the first to come through[NOTE:1] the doors of my house to meet me when I return safely from fighting the Ammonites—he[NOTE:2] will belong to the Lord, and[NOTE:3] I will offer him up as a burnt sacrifice.”
notes: Heb “the one coming out, who comes out from.” The text uses a masculine singular participle with prefixed article, followed by a relative pronoun and third masculine singular verb. The substantival masculine singular participle הַיּוֹצֵא (hayyotseʾ, “the one coming out”) is used elsewhere of inanimate objects (such as a desert [Num 21:13] or a word [Num 32:24]) or persons (Jer 5:6; 21:9; 38:2). In each case context must determine the referent. Jephthah may have envisioned an animal meeting him, since the construction of Iron Age houses would allow for an animal coming through the doors of a house (see R. G. Boling, Judges [AB], 208). But the fact that he actually does offer up his daughter indicates the language of the vow is fluid enough to encompass human beings, including women. He probably intended such an offering from the very beginning, but he obviously did not expect his daughter to meet him first.
The language is fluid enough to include women and perhaps even animals, but the translation uses the masculine pronoun because the Hebrew form is grammatically masculine.

Some translate “or,” suggesting that Jephthah makes a distinction between humans and animals. According to this view, if a human comes through the door, then Jephthah will commit him/her to the Lord’s service, but if an animal comes through the doors, he will offer it up as a sacrifice. However, it is far more likely that the Hebrew construction (vav [ו] + perfect) specifies how the subject will become the Lord’s, that is, by being offered up as a sacrifice. For similar constructions, where the apodosis of a conditional sentence has at least two perfects (each with vav) in sequence, see Gen 34:15-16; Exod 18:16.

verses.zh: 于是耶弗他往亚扪人那里去，与他们争战；耶和华将他们交在他手中，
verses.en: Jephthah approached[NOTE:1] the Ammonites to fight with them, and the Lord handed them over to him.
notes: Heb “passed over to.”

verses.zh: 他就大大杀败他们，从亚罗珥到米匿，直到亚备勒・基拉明，攻取了二十座城。这样亚扪人就被以色列人制伏了。
verses.en: He defeated them from Aroer all the way to Minnith—20 cities in all, even as far as Abel Keramim. He wiped them out![NOTE:1] The Israelites humiliated the Ammonites.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “with a very great slaughter.”
Heb “The Ammonites were humbled before the Israelites.”

verses.zh: 耶弗他回米斯巴到了自己的家，不料，他女儿拿着鼓跳舞出来迎接他，是他独生的，此外无儿无女。
verses.en: When Jephthah came home to Mizpah, there was his daughter hurrying out[NOTE:1] to meet him, dancing to the rhythm of tambourines.[NOTE:2] She was his only child; except for her he had no son or daughter.
notes: Heb “Look! His daughter was coming out.”
Heb “with tambourines and dancing.”

verses.zh: 耶弗他看见她，就撕裂衣服，说：「哀哉！我的女儿啊，你使我甚是愁苦，叫我作难了；因为我已经向耶和华开口许愿，不能挽回。」
verses.en: When he saw her, he ripped his clothes and said, “Oh no! My daughter! You have completely ruined me![NOTE:1] You have brought me disaster![NOTE:2] I made an oath to the Lord, and I cannot break it.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you have brought me very low,” or “you have knocked me to my knees.” The infinitive absolute precedes the verb for emphasis.
Heb “You are among [or “like”] those who trouble me.”
Heb “I opened my mouth to the Lord and I am not able to return.”

verses.zh: 他女儿回答说：「父啊，你既向耶和华开口，就当照你口中所说的向我行，因耶和华已经在仇敌亚扪人身上为你报仇」；
verses.en: She said to him, “My father, since[NOTE:1] you made an oath to the Lord, do to me as you promised.[NOTE:2] After all, the Lord vindicated you before[NOTE:3] your enemies, the Ammonites.”
notes: The conjunction “since” is supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “you opened your mouth to the Lord, do to me according to [what] went out from your mouth.”
Or “has given you vengeance against.”

verses.zh: 又对父亲说：「有一件事求你允准：容我去两个月，与同伴在山上，好哀哭我终为处女。」
verses.en: She then said to her father, “Please grant me this one wish.[NOTE:1] For two months allow me to walk through the hills with my friends and mourn my virginity.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Let this thing be done for me.”
Heb “Leave me alone for two months so I can go and go down on the hills and weep over my virginity—I and my friends.”

verses.zh: 耶弗他说：「你去吧！」就容她去两个月。她便和同伴去了，在山上为她终为处女哀哭。
verses.en: He said, “You may go.” He permitted her to leave[NOTE:1] for two months. She went with her friends and mourned her virginity as she walked through the hills.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he sent her.”
Heb “on the hills.” The words “as she walked” are supplied.

verses.zh: 两月已满，她回到父亲那里，父亲就照所许的愿向她行了。女儿终身没有亲近男子。
verses.en: After two months she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. She died a virgin.[NOTE:1] Her tragic death gave rise to a custom in Israel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “She had never known a man.” Some understand this to mean that her father committed her to a life of celibacy, but the disjunctive clause (note the vav + subject + verb pattern) more likely describes her condition at the time the vow was fulfilled. (See G. F. Moore, Judges [ICC], 302-3; C. F. Burney, Judges, 324.) She died a virgin and never experienced the joys of marriage and motherhood.
Heb “There was a custom in Israel.”

verses.zh: 此后以色列中有个规矩，每年以色列的女子去为基列人耶弗他的女儿哀哭四天。
verses.en: Every year[NOTE:1] Israelite women commemorate[NOTE:2] the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite for four days.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “From days to days,” a Hebrew idiom for “annually.”
Heb “go to commemorate.” The rare Hebrew verb תָּנָה (tanah, “to tell; to repeat; to recount”) occurs only here and in 5:11.
The Hebrew text adds, “in the year.” This is redundant (note “every year” at the beginning of the verse) and has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 11:1-3

1Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a valiant warrior, but he was the son of a harlot. And Gilead
was the father of Jephthah. 2Gilead's wife bore him sons; and when his wife's sons grew up, they
drove Jephthah out and said to him, "You shall not have an inheritance in our father's house, for you are the son
of another woman." 3So Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob; and worthless
fellows gathered themselves about Jephthah, and they went out with him.

11:1 "Jephthah" His name means "He (God) opens" (BDB 836, possibly "God opens the womb"). See
note about him in Heb. 11:37.

▣ "the Gileadite" The name "Gilead" (BDB 167) is used for

- the hill country of northeast Jordan (BDB 166), which was the tribal allocation of Reuben and Gad (Deut. 3:12)

- an ADJECTIVE for a person living in northeast trans-Jordan (BDB 167) between the Arnon and
Jabbok Rivers, Jdgs. 11:1

- the proper name of a person (BDB 167, #6), Jdgs. 11:1

▣ "a valiant warrior" This was used by the angel to describe Gideon (cf. Jdgs. 6:12). It could denote

- fighting courage and ability

- nobility of some type (wealth, influence, social standing, see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, p. 70; quotes
Jos. 8:30; Ruth 2:1; 1 Sam. 9:1; 2 Kgs. 15:20; 24:14)

▣ "harlot"This (BDB 275, KB 278) was a socially unacceptable union within Israel. A concubine was
a socially acceptable union but still not a full legal wife (i.e., limited inheritance). Jephthah's mother was probably
Canaanite. Jephthah had no inheritance rights (cf. Jdgs. 11:3).

▣ "the father of" This phrase is really from one VERB "begot" (BDB 408, KB 411,
Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw).

11:3 "Tob" This word (BDB 376 IV) means "good" or "fruitful," possibly northeast in Gilead on the eastern
side of the Jordan.

▣ "worthless fellows" This refers to mercenaries. This was much like David's early life (i.e., 1 Sam. 22:1-2).
It shows Jephthah was a leader of men; those without hope or social standing rallied to him.

Josephus (Antiq. 5.7.8) says they asked for Jephthah's help because he maintained an army (i.e.,
"worthless fellows") at his own expense.

The problem is the wide semantical field of the Hebrew ADVERB

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE RED SEA

▣ "Kadesh" This was a large desert oasis in the southern part of Judah's allocation in the wilderness of
Paran, where Israel camped so long (cf. Num. 13:26; 20:1; Deut. 1:19-25).

11:17 "Edom" Edomites were relatives of the Israelites from Esau (cf. Num. 20:14-21; Deut. 2:5-8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDOM AND ISRAEL

▣ "Moab" These were relatives of the Israelites from Lot (cf. Gen. 19:36-38), as is Ammon (cf. Deut.
2:19, 27). Ammon was not well established during the conquest era but by the time of the Judges they were.

11:19 "Heshbon" Heshbon is located on the "King's Highway" and was Sihon's capital (cf. Num. 21:26).

11:20 "trust" This term (BDB 52, KB 63, Hiphil PERFECT) basically meant "to confirm"
of "to support." It is an important theological word.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH, AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OLD TESTAMENT

controller of history.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

11:23 "Chemosh" This was the god of Moab, not the Ammonites. From Ugaritic a connection has been
found between Molech and Chemosh through Anath-Chemosh.

11:24 The NASB Study Bible, p. 330, suggests that because Chemosh was the chief deity of the Moabites,
not the Canaanites:

- at this time, Ammon ruled Moab

- at this time, there was a confederation between Ammon and Moab.

PARTICIPLE

PERFECT

PERFECT

11:26 "Aroer" It was a region associated with the Arnon River.

▣ "three hundred years" This seems too long! The Jewish Study Bible, p. 537, thinks this refers to the
